deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no formulas, no derivations, no computations. It is a heavily corrected prose draft of an official report (Gutachten) for the Royal Hanoverian Government. The report responds to Gen. Lt. J. J. Baeyer's proposal of 1861 for a 'Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung', the Central European arc measurement. The previous and next pages belong to the same draft.

Content of the page:
(1) Comparing astronomical with geodetic longitude and latitude determinations, in order to fix the figure of the Earth more precisely, is a self-contained scientific investigation. It does not require several parties to cooperate.
(2) A struck-out sentence began to point to a further investigation. The previous page shows what Riemann had in mind: using pendulum (gravity) observations to supplement the Hanoverian arc measurement, so as to determine deflections of the vertical (Lothabweichungen).
(3) A fragment starts, 'Die genauere Bestimmung der Gestalt der Erde durch d.[?]', and is abandoned.
(4) Riemann concludes that for this part of Baeyer's undertaking, the Hanoverian Government's participation does not come into question.
(5) He then begins: 'Es möge jedoch gestattet sein...', and a separate line: 'Zur Förderung des Zwecks der Gradmessungen wichtige Beiträge geliefert werden könnten'. The sentence is left unfinished.

The page's place in the argument: the next page divides the task into three parts. These are (i) the purely geodetic positions of the stations on the reference ellipsoid; (ii) the astronomical longitude and latitude differences; and (iii) their comparison. This page discusses part (iii) and the possible Hanoverian role. The underlying scientific idea is gravimetric determination of deflections of the vertical, following Gauss's remark and Airy's studies. It is described only qualitatively; no formula or method is worked out.

results.what: Statement that the astronomical-geodetic comparison (deflections of the vertical) for determining the Earth's figure is a self-contained investigation not requiring cooperation. Implied suggestion (from the previous page) to supplement the Hanoverian arc measurement with pendulum gravity observations.
results.modern_name: Astrogeodetic determination of the geoid / deflections of the vertical; gravimetric (Stokes / Vening-Meinesz type) determination of deflections
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (remarks on the plumb-line deviation), Airy, Pratt (1850s); Stokes 1849 for the gravimetric formula; Vening Meinesz 1928 for gravimetric deflections

deep.surprise_reason: This is administrative and expository prose from Riemann's draft report on Baeyer's Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung, with no mathematical content. That Riemann was consulted on this project is at least plausibly known, but I am unsure how well it is documented in the secondary literature. The ideas (deflections of the vertical, pendulum observations) were standard for geodesy around 1861.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the struck word before 'Längenbestimmungen' appears to be 'Breiten', with 'und' inserted; that reading is consistent with the machine transcription. The phrase reads 'astronomischen [Breiten-] und Längenbestimmungen'.
Line 2: after 'Erde bildet' there is a short struck mark, probably an abandoned letter, not a word.

The struck passage beginning '; bei diesem Theile' contains the superscript insertion 'und es wird daher'. The struck word before 'von Hrn. Gen. Lt. Baeyer' looks like 'Untern[ehmens]' (the image may read 'Untern' or 'Untersu'), rendered roughly 'Unterne[?]' in the transcription.
The final fragment reads 'Zur Förderung des Zwecks der Gradmessungen [die] wichtige / Beiträge geliefert werden könnten', or possibly 'könnte'; the sentence is unfinished.
